# Code

RLinf's design patterns are in [patterns.md](patterns.md), and the rules CI and reviewers enforce are in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). This skill says what to read before you change code and checks the change afterwards. Install, Docker, and e2e wiring for a new model or env belong to the [install](../install/SKILL.md) skill, and docs and README highlights to the [docs](../docs/SKILL.md) skill.

## Write

1. Find the closest current sibling on `main` and start from it: the newest model under `rlinf/models/embodiment/`, env under `rlinf/envs/`, or runner, worker, or algorithm of the same kind. `git log <base> -- <dir>` shows which one is recent, so you copy current conventions rather than legacy boilerplate.
2. Plug into the extension point the component kind already has, from the table in AGENTS.md § Extending RLinf, instead of adding a branch to shared code.
3. Read [patterns.md](patterns.md): its design philosophy first, then the Design, Code, and Tests patterns that apply to the change.
4. Put new tests in the component's existing file in `tests/unit_tests/`, through the public contract, and mock only what lies outside RLinf (patterns.md § Tests).
5. Start a new config YAML from the closest current one in `examples/`, keep values static, and override only what differs from the Hydra `defaults` (patterns.md § Configuration).
6. Add every new `.py`, test, or root YAML file to the path filter in `.github/workflows/ci-tests.yml` whose tests exercise it.
7. Before you finish, go through [mistakes.md](mistakes.md), the mistakes agents most often make in RLinf code, then run the check below and the unit tests of the component you changed (AGENTS.md § Setup and commands).

## Check

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/code/check.py              # files changed against main
python3 .agents/skills/code/check.py FILE ...
```

It prints findings in the shared format of [README.md](../README.md#findings):

| Rule | Severity | Reports |
|---|---|---|
| `code/pre-commit` | major | `pre-commit run --files` fails: Ruff lint and format, and the license header where Ruff applies. Ruff runs with `--fix`, so run the check again after it rewrites a file. |
| `code/init` | major | a directory under `rlinf/` with Python files and no `__init__.py` |
| `code/license` | major or minor | a new Python file without `# Copyright <year> The RLinf Authors.` (major), or with a year other than the current one (minor) |
| `code/ci-filter` | major | a changed file that CI's `filter-coverage-test` would reject |
| `code/test-layout` | minor | a new file in `tests/unit_tests/` |

Then go through what a script cannot decide, for every changed function, compared with its version on `main`. [mistakes.md](mistakes.md) lists the concrete forms these take:

- [ ] The change extends an existing mechanism; shared code gains no branch that names a model, env, or accelerator (patterns.md § Generalize; don't special-case, § Contain component code).
- [ ] Each resource has one owner, and the fix sits at the layer that owns the invariant (§ Small abstractions with one owner, § Fix at the owning layer).
- [ ] No protection code for states the caller cannot produce, and validation happens once at the boundary (§ No unnecessary protection code).
- [ ] Behavior is preserved on every affected backend, env, model, and task, or the difference is named, documented, and tested (§ Preserve behavior).
- [ ] No new function, field, or config key without a caller or consumer, and no changed line that does not serve the change.
- [ ] Code conventions hold: logging through `self.log_*` or `get_logger()`, `self.torch_platform` instead of `torch.cuda`, type hints and Google-style docstrings on public APIs, short comments, and messages that say what was expected and what was found (§ Code).
- [ ] Tests fail without the change, use real objects, mock only the process edge, and carry `@pytest.mark.placement` when they host parts in scheduler workers (§ Tests).

---
name: create-pr
description: Open a GitHub pull request for RLinf, or fix an existing one — checks the PR title against Conventional Commits, writes a precise description that follows .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md, and lints both before pushing. # Create a PR

Write the title and the description, then **run the linter before you post**:

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/create-pr/lint_pr.py lint \
    --title "fix(libero): reset action queues between episodes" \
    --body-file /tmp/pr-body.md
```

Exit code 1 means at least one ERROR — fix it and re-run. It is the same
checker you point at a PR that is already open:

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/create-pr/lint_pr.py lint --pr 1444
```

The rules come from [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) ("PR Title and
Description"), [.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md](../../../.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md),
and — for the title — the required `pr-title-check` job, which runs
[`openGemini/pr-title-checker`](https://github.com/openGemini/pr-title-checker)
with `strict: true`. Every title rule that job enforces is an ERROR in the
linter, so a clean `lint` means the check passes. Paths below are relative to
the repo root.

## 1. Gather the facts before writing a word

Never describe the PR from memory of what you intended. Read the diff:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD
git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD
```

You need, concretely:

- **Which component the diff touches** — that becomes the scope.
- **Every user-visible change** — a new config key, a renamed flag, a moved doc
  page, a changed default. Internal churn does not go in the description.
- **What you actually ran to verify it** — the e2e config name, the eval
  numbers, `pre-commit run --all-files`. "Tested locally" is not an answer.
- **The issue it closes**, if any.

Then run the check of every area the branch touches, and fix each finding or
say in the description why it stays:

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/route.py check
```

Its result goes into `How has this been tested?` with the other commands you
ran.

## 2. Title

```
<type>(<scope>): <description>
```

- **type**: `feat` `fix` `docs` `style` `refactor` `test` `chore` `perf`
  `build` `ci` `revert`. Lowercase. On `main` the distribution is roughly
  `feat` 166 / `fix` 122 / `docs` 76 / `chore` 18 / `refactor` 14.
- **scope**: the component the diff touches — `embodiment`, `libero`,
  `realworld`, `readme`, `docker`, `collective`, `openpi_pytorch`. Optional;
  drop it rather than invent one. `[a-z0-9_-]` only — a space, slash, dot or
  capital fails CI. `feat(new)` (PR #1421) passes CI but is the anti-pattern
  the linter warns on: it names the PR, not the code.
- **description**: **≤ 50 characters**, and that is the part *after* `: `, not
  the whole title. This is the rule PRs fail most often. It must start with a
  lowercase `a-z` (so `support 5D parallelism`, never `5D parallelism
  support`), stay imperative, carry no trailing period, and use plain ASCII —
  `π₀` in a title fails the check.
  `add MolmoAct2 LIBERO evaluation support`, not `Added support for MolmoAct2`.
- Never append `(#123)` — GitHub adds it at squash-merge.

Fitting 50 characters is the whole discipline of the title: name the one change
a reviewer needs to see in the PR list, and let the body carry the rest. If the
PR does several things, title it after the largest and enumerate in
`Description`.

Check just the title, no body needed:

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/create-pr/lint_pr.py lint --title "feat(new): add stuff."
```

## 3. Body

Start from the skeleton so no section goes missing:

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/create-pr/lint_pr.py template > /tmp/pr-body.md
```

Then fill it in. **Keep all six headings**, even where a section is one line.
What each one is for:

| Section | What goes in it |
| --- | --- |
| `Description` | One sentence on what changed and where, then a bullet per user-visible change. ≤ 250 words, ≤ 12 bullets. |
| `Motivation and Context` | Why the change is needed. Link the issue (`Fixes #NNN`). |
| `How has this been tested?` | The command you ran and its outcome. Required by CONTRIBUTING.md when the PR can move the reward curve — give the numbers. |
| `Additional information` | Figures, logs, repro commands. May be empty. |
| `Types of changes` | Tick what applies. One or two boxes, not four. |
| `Checklist:` | Tick what applies. **CONTRIBUTING.md: a PR with an empty Description or Checklist is marked draft and not reviewed.** |

Style rules the linter enforces:

- **No leading indentation.** Not on headings, not on paragraphs, not on table
  rows. Four spaces turns a paragraph into a code block; a table whose header
  and rows disagree on indent does not render as a table at all.
- **Delete the `<!--- ... -->` hints** once a section is written.
- **Nothing above the first `###` heading** — put it in `Description`.
- **One line per paragraph.** GitHub reflows; hard wraps only survive until
  someone edits the body.

## 4. Lint, then create

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/create-pr/lint_pr.py lint \
    --title "$TITLE" --body-file /tmp/pr-body.md
```

Add `--docs-only` for a documentation-only PR to drop the "how was this tested"
warning. Add `--quiet` to omit the suggested fixes. Once it exits 0:

```bash
gh pr create --base main --title "$TITLE" --body-file /tmp/pr-body.md
```

Commits must be signed off (`git commit -s`) and follow the same
`<type>(<scope>): <description>` format — DCO checks the trailer, so make sure
your name is not wrapped in quotes.

## 5. Fixing a PR that is already open

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/create-pr/lint_pr.py lint --pr 1421
```

For the indent/wrap damage specifically, `fix` rewrites the body: it strips the
paste offset (preserving genuine list nesting), pulls headings and tables flush
left, and drops the template hints. `--unwrap` additionally joins hard-wrapped
prose into one line per paragraph.

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/create-pr/lint_pr.py fix --pr 1421 --unwrap > /tmp/fixed.md
python3 .agents/skills/create-pr/lint_pr.py lint --title "$TITLE" --body-file /tmp/fixed.md
gh pr edit 1421 --body-file /tmp/fixed.md
gh pr edit 1421 --title "feat(embodiment): add MolmoAct2 LIBERO evaluation support"
```

`fix` only de-indents a body the linter already flagged, so running it on a
well-formed PR is a no-op apart from comment removal. **Read the output before
posting it** — it is a mechanical rewrite, not an editor.

## Gotchas

- **`lint --pr N` shells out to `gh pr view`**, so it inherits your `gh` auth
  and the repo you are standing in. It is read-only; nothing is posted until
  you run `gh pr edit` / `gh pr create` yourself.
- **The skeleton from `template` fails its own lint** — deliberately. It ships
  with no boxes ticked, and `checkbox-unticked` is an ERROR. Tick them.
- **The linter accepts `##` as well as `###`** for section headings, because
  GitHub renders both. What it will not accept is a *renamed* section: a body
  using `## Testing` instead of `### How has this been tested?` reports
  `section-missing`.
- **Warnings do not fail the run** (exit 0). `body-hardwrap`, `body-comments`
  and `title-scope-vague` are judgement calls — but a reviewer reads them the
  same way the linter does.
- **`fix` cannot recover a broken code fence.** If `body-fence` fires (odd
  number of ```` ``` ````), everything after the stray fence has been swallowed
  by GitHub's renderer; find it and close it by hand.
- **Tables inside `<details>` still need flush-left rows.** The `<details>`
  wrapper does not exempt them.
- **A good commit subject is not always a legal PR title.** `commit-check` and
  `pr-title-check` are different jobs with different limits — commit subjects
  get ~72 characters, PR descriptions get 50. A one-commit PR that reuses its
  subject verbatim can fail.

## Troubleshooting

- `error: gh pr view N failed: ... could not resolve to a PullRequest` — wrong
  repo. `cd` to the RLinf checkout, or pass the number of a PR in this repo.
- `[E] body/body-indented` persists after `fix` — the body mixes two paste
  offsets (e.g. part typed, part pasted). Dedent by hand; `fix` only removes a
  single uniform offset.
- `[W] body/section-order` — you kept all the headings but reordered them.
  Harmless, but reviewers scan for the template order.
- `lint --title` alone reports `0 error(s)` on an empty body — that is correct,
  it only checks what you gave it. Pass `--body-file` too before you create.

Holds the writing rules split by page type (recipe, guide, concept, extending, reference, index, publication) and by language, the mistakes agents make in docs, templates, and the check for the build, markup, names, EN/ZH parity, and writing. ---

# Docs

RLinf's documentation rules live in [rules/](rules/), split so that a writer reads only what the page in hand needs: the rules for every page, the rules for its type, and the rules for each language. This file says which to read, how to write a page, and how to check it.

## Write

1. **Classify the page** by where it lives ([rules/base.md](rules/base.md) has the table), and open a current page of the same type in the same section, or its template in [templates/](templates/).
2. **Read** [rules/base.md](rules/base.md), the file for the page type, [rules/english.md](rules/english.md) and [rules/chinese.md](rules/chinese.md) for the languages you write, and [rules/glossary.md](rules/glossary.md) for terms.
3. **Check the facts** the page will state against the code: every command, config key, path, and model or env name.
4. **Plan the page**: its type, its reader, the result the reader reaches, and one line per section saying what it answers.
5. **Write the English and the Chinese page from the plan**, each in its own language. Write the Chinese from the plan, not by translating the English sentences.
6. **Place the page** in one gallery or section index and in both toctrees ([rules/index.md](rules/index.md)), and add a README highlight for a feature worth announcing ([rules/readme.md](rules/readme.md)).
7. **Go through [rules/mistakes.md](rules/mistakes.md).**
8. **Run a simplicity and language pass.** Give a fresh agent, which has seen nothing else, only the changed pages, [rules/base.md](rules/base.md), and the language file for each. Ask it first to cut anything the reader does not need for the main path (long-winded explanations of details, redundant paragraphs, repeated facts, restated YAML defaults, defensive caveats, code citations, complex commands, dense inline parameter dumps, and repeated negative-and-positive framing such as "this is not A, not B, but C"), and then to rewrite any remaining sentence that reads as translated, padded, or built on code names. Apply the cuts and rewrites that hold. A writer cannot hear the length or cadence of their own prose.
9. **Run the check** below and fix what it reports.

### A recipe page for a new model or env

- Write `docs/source-en/rst_source/examples/embodied/<name>.rst` and the same path under `docs/source-zh/`, from [templates/recipe.rst](templates/recipe.rst) and [templates/recipe.zh.rst](templates/recipe.zh.rst). Agentic recipes live under `examples/agentic/`, system demos under `examples/system/`.
- Register the page in the gallery index that owns it ([rules/index.md § Where a page goes](rules/index.md#where-a-page-goes)), with its card and its entry in the hidden toctree, in both languages.
- When the env has a benchmark evaluation flow, link it from the matching page under `evaluations/`.

### A publication page

Write `resources/publications/<slug>.rst` in both languages from [templates/publication.rst](templates/publication.rst), following [rules/publication.md](rules/publication.md), then add its row to the `list-table` in `publications/index.rst` and its slug to the hidden toctree, in both languages.

## Check

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/docs/check.py              # docs changed against main
python3 .agents/skills/docs/check.py FILE ...     # specific pages
python3 .agents/skills/docs/check.py --no-build   # skip the Sphinx build while iterating
```

Page findings count only on the lines the change adds, because many existing pages predate the current rules; `--all-lines` reports every line of the selected pages, for a cleanup pass. The build always covers both trees. The build and the markup check run in the docs virtualenv: `$DOCS_VENV`, or `<repo>/.docs-venv`, which the script creates from `requirements/docs/requirements.txt` on first use. Findings use the shared format of [../README.md](../README.md#findings):

| `docs/tab-parity` | major | paired EN/ZH pages with mismatched `.. tab-set::` or `.. tab-item::` counts |
| `docs/mirror-comment` | major | commented `--use-mirror`, `HF_ENDPOINT`, `hf-mirror`, or `gh-proxy` lines inside bash blocks |

| `docs/inline-code-density` | minor | single prose paragraph packing >= 6 inline code literals (`` ``...`` ``) on a recipe or guide page; simplify or move into a table/dropdown |

| `docs/alpha-order` | major | unsorted simulator, real-world robot, model, RL method, Agent & LLM sub-category, algorithm reference, Python API, or publication toctrees (`simulators_index`, `vla_wam_index`, `sft_index`, `world_model_index`, `video_models`, `methods_index`, `agentic/{math_reasoning,agents}/index`, `reference/{algorithms,api}/index`, `resources/publications/index`, and root `Real-World Robots`) |

- [ ] The checklist in the page type's rules file holds.
- [ ] **Readability & conciseness**: apply [rules/base.md](rules/base.md#prefer-simplicity-and-readability-over-verbosity). Flag unreadable/stiff prose, machine-translated or sentence-by-sentence Chinese, long-winded detail explanations, walls of prose, internal code citations, repeated facts, restated YAML defaults, repeated negative-and-positive framing ("not A, not B, but C" / "不是……而是……"), and pages bloatier than a clean `main` sibling covering the same scope.
- [ ] **Commands & sibling alignment (recipes/guides)**: compare against the closest model- or domain-family siblings on `main` (not only the gallery). Shared setup links to existing family pages or partials; commands stay minimal and YAML-first (no shell plumbing, long CLI overrides, inline prep scripts, or env-var workarounds).
- [ ] **Docs ↔ code accuracy**: every config key, flag, env var, path, and model/env name matches `main` plus the change; public additions, renames, or removals update all affected EN/ZH pages.
- [ ] **Cross-references**: a sentence that sends the reader to another page for a step ("as in", "see") points to a page that covers that step for the same model, config, and workflow. Open the target page; a link that resolves is not enough.
- [ ] **Code examples**: code the reader is meant to copy (a subclass, a hook, a config snippet) runs as shown. When it needs a cluster, trace each of its branches against the code of the change, including the error and early-exit branches, and confirm each one ends in a state RLinf accepts.
- [ ] **Parity, assets & README**: paired EN/ZH pages agree on sections, commands, keys, claims, and numbers; changed assets pass [reference.md § Asset references](reference.md#asset-references); noteworthy features get a README highlight ([rules/readme.md](rules/readme.md)).
- [ ] None of the mistakes in [rules/mistakes.md](rules/mistakes.md) remains.

Report each changed page with its type and result (pass or findings). Rate a page `major` when it fails any of the bullets above as a whole (hard to follow or run, bloated/unscannable, machine-translated Chinese, cites internals instead of behavior, complex/non-standard commands, duplicated setup, or broken parity/placement); rate isolated wording issues `minor`. Quote the line, name the rule, and give the rewrite.

# Install

`requirements/install.sh` installs every embodied model and env combination, `docker/Dockerfile` builds an image per target, and the e2e workflows install a target and train it for a few steps on a CI runner. This skill covers adding a target to all three, the conventions the install script follows, a check for changes to it, and a driver that builds the venv and runs the e2e test the way CI does. All paths are relative to the repository root, and [reference.md](reference.md) has the code shapes.

## Conventions

1. **Reuse the common utilities.** If one almost fits, extend it rather than writing a near-duplicate.

   | Need | Use | Instead of |
   |---|---|---|
   | Clone a repo | `clone_or_reuse_repo ENV_VAR DEFAULT_DIR URL [git args…]` (reuse through `*_PATH`, mirror prefix, re-clone when corrupt) | raw `git clone` |
   | flash-attn | `install_flash_attn` (platform-aware, prebuilt wheels, source fallback) | hand-built wheel URLs |
   | apex | `install_apex` | building apex inline |
   | venv and base sync | `create_and_sync_venv`, then `install_common_embodied_deps` | `uv venv` or `uv sync` by hand |
   | A torch version | the `--torch` flag, applied by `apply_torch_override` | `sed` on `pyproject.toml` |
   | System libs, EGL, Vulkan | `requirements/embodied/sys_deps.sh` and the per-platform render config | `apt-get`, or ICD JSON written inline |
   | CUDA or ROCm version | `detect_cuda_major_minor`, `detect_rocm_version` | parsing `nvcc` or `rocminfo` |
   | Mirror-aware git | the `GITHUB_PREFIX` prefix and `setup_mirror` | hardcoded mirror URLs |

2. **One `install_<model>_model()` per model**, which `case`s on `$ENV_NAME` and calls the matching `install_<env>_env()`. An env with no model installs through a branch in `install_env_only`.
3. **System packages go in `requirements/embodied/sys_deps.sh`**, added to every `install_deps_<manager>` function so apt, dnf, yum, and pacman hosts all get them. `install.sh` never calls a package manager.
4. **Every git dependency is pinned** to a commit, tag, or branch (`@<rev>` or `-b <branch>`), or forked into `github.com/RLinf/<repo>`.
5. **RLinf's own `pyproject.toml` changes only through `apply_torch_override`.** When an override conflicts with a dependency, `cd` into that dependency's checkout and install from there; editing the cloned repo's `pyproject.toml` after the `cd` is fine.
6. **Core dependencies stay as they are.** Never pin `ray` per env, and avoid loose `torch` pins. Before adding `uv pip install x==y`, check whether the common deps or `pyproject.toml` already provide it.
7. **A new model or env gets a Docker stage** when comparable targets on `main` have one. Real-world hardware envs (`yam`, `so101`, `piper`, `dosw1`, `gim_arm`, `xsquare_turtle2`) have none.
8. **Keep it small.** A short `case` branch that calls shared helpers beats a long block of `sed` and `uv pip` workarounds.

## Write

### Add a model or env

1. **Install script.** Add the name to `SUPPORTED_MODELS` or `SUPPORTED_ENVS`.
   - A new model gets `install_<model>_model()` and a `<model>)` branch in the `case "$MODEL"` of `main()`. Model-specific pins go in `requirements/embodied/models/<model>.txt` once there are more than a couple.
   - A new env for an existing model is a branch in that model's `case "$ENV_NAME"` that calls `create_and_sync_venv`, `install_common_embodied_deps`, and `install_<env>_env`; the model's own packages install after the `case`.
   - An env with no model is a branch in `install_env_only`.
2. **Dockerfile.** Add a `base-image-embodied-<target>` line if the target needs another base, and a `FROM embodied-common-image AS embodied-<target>-image` stage that runs `install.sh` and sets the default venv in `~/.bashrc`. A stage that installs several venvs chains every `install.sh` call in one `RUN` with `&&`, because uv hardlinks from its cache only within one layer. The new stage is a valid `BUILD_TARGET` with no change to the final stage.
3. **Docker build CI.** Copy a `build-embodied-*` job in `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml` and change the job id, step name, `BUILD_TARGET`, and tag.
4. **E2e test.** Add `tests/e2e_tests/embodied/<env>_<algo>_<model>.yaml`, started from a current sibling and following the code skill's config rules ([patterns.md § Configuration](../code/patterns.md#configuration)). Add a job to `.github/workflows/embodied-e2e-tests.yml` that installs the target, runs `tests/e2e_tests/embodied/run.sh <config>` (or `run_async.sh`), and removes `.venv`. Jobs run on `runs-on: embodied`, and none runs `uv cache prune` against the shared cache.
5. **Path filters and docs.** New files go into the path filters of `.github/workflows/ci-tests.yml` ([code](../code/SKILL.md)), and the model or env gets its recipe page and README highlight ([docs](../docs/SKILL.md)).

Run `bash -n requirements/install.sh` after each edit, and the check below before you finish.

## Check

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/install/check.py            # files changed against main
python3 .agents/skills/install/check.py FILE ...
```

The line rules report only the lines the change adds to `install.sh`, and the Docker stage rule only the names it adds, so exceptions already on `main` do not repeat; `--all-lines` audits the whole file instead. The rules are heuristics: each hit is a line to review against the conventions. Findings use the shared format of [README.md](../README.md#findings):

| Rule | Severity | Reports |
|---|---|---|
| `install/syntax` | critical | a shell script under `requirements/` that fails `bash -n` |
| `install/sys-deps` | major | a package-manager call in `install.sh` (convention 3) |
| `install/git-pin` | major | a git dependency neither pinned nor forked into RLinf (convention 4) |
| `install/core-dep` | major or minor | a `ray` pin (major) or an explicit `torch` pin (minor) (convention 6) |
| `install/pyproject` | minor | a write to a `pyproject.toml` outside `apply_torch_override` (convention 5) |
| `install/clone` | minor | a raw `git clone` (convention 1) |
| `install/docker-stage` | major | a model or env added to `SUPPORTED_*` with no `--model` or `--env` install in the Dockerfile (convention 7) |
| `install/docker-layers` | major | a changed Docker stage that calls `install.sh` from more than one `RUN` |
| `install/e2e-wiring` | major | a new e2e config that no workflow runs |

Some hits are sanctioned: a `torch` pin installed from `~` inside `pushd ~ … popd`, a clone that a later `git checkout <hash>` in the same function pins, a multi-repo build such as the Franka catkin workspace, and an edit to a cloned repo's `pyproject.toml` after `cd` into it. Keep such a line and say why in the PR.

Then judge what the script cannot:

- [ ] The change is a small branch that calls shared helpers, and each new override is one a common dependency does not already provide.
- [ ] A new Docker image, model, or dataset comes with a maintainer ping in the PR.
- [ ] A new e2e job does not duplicate coverage another workflow already runs.
- [ ] Install, Docker, or CI changes stay within what the new component needs.

## Verify

[driver.py](driver.py) reads the install command, env vars, and test configs from `.github/workflows/embodied-e2e-tests.yml`, so it reproduces CI without a copy that drifts. It runs on the embodied CI runner or an equivalent host: NVIDIA GPUs, the shared `/workspace/dataset/` tree, `uv`, and a `python3` with PyYAML (it re-runs itself under `uv run --with pyyaml` otherwise).

Start with the read-only subcommands, which return at once:

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/install/driver.py list                       # combos CI covers and their configs
python3 .agents/skills/install/driver.py resolve <model> <env>      # CI's install command, env vars, configs
python3 .agents/skills/install/driver.py check-paths <config>       # do the config's model paths exist here?
python3 .agents/skills/install/driver.py check-all                  # check-paths over every e2e config
```

`check-paths` classifies each absolute path as `[model/input]` (must exist), `[output dir]` (created by the run), or `[path]` (informational). A missing `[model/input]` fails the run before training; on a host without the dataset tree that is a staging gap, not an install bug.

`run` installs, checks paths, and runs the test. Preview it with `--dry-run`, which prints the exact shell, then drop the flag:

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/install/driver.py run <model> <env> --venv /workspace/test-venvs/<model> --dry-run
python3 .agents/skills/install/driver.py install <model> <env> --venv /workspace/test-venvs/<model>
python3 .agents/skills/install/driver.py test <config> --venv /workspace/test-venvs/<model>
```

`install` and `test` run the two halves separately, so one install serves many tests. A run is done when fresh TensorBoard files appear under the config's `log_path`. Afterwards `rm -rf` the `--venv` you built unless the user wants to keep it; leave the shared uv caches and the prebuilt `/opt/venv/*` alone. When a model or env has no e2e job, ask the user what to run; `test <config> --runner run|run_async|run_offline` runs a config that CI does not. [reference.md § Driver notes](reference.md#driver-notes) has the gotchas and the troubleshooting.

## When to stop and ask

Ask the user when a dependency conflicts with a core pin and neither a pin, a fork, nor a `cd` workaround is clearly right; when the set of envs a model supports is unclear; or when it is unclear whether a target should ship a Docker image. A wrong pin or a missing image breaks installs or CI for every other env.

description: Reviews an RLinf pull request for correctness, design, and code reuse against RLinf's design patterns, runs the check of every area the PR touches (code, docs, install) through those skills and the reproduction when the host can, reports concise, deduplicated findings with evidence, and, when the user asks, posts them as one GitHub review. # Review a PR

Produce one concise, deduplicated review in the step 8 format: a verdict, a two-bullet reproduction summary, the findings table, detail sections only for non-inline (`here`) findings, inline comments printed once, and a two-bullet check summary (not posted). Post to GitHub only when the user asks ([posting.md](posting.md)).

Focus on correctness, design, reuse, and unnecessary divergence from `main`. Area checks live in [code](../code/SKILL.md), [docs](../docs/SKILL.md), and [install](../install/SKILL.md). Read [code/patterns.md](../code/patterns.md) and [reference.md](reference.md) before step 5.

## 1. Set up

Cross-reference against `main` of `github.com/RLinf/RLinf`, never the local working tree:

```bash
N=<PR number>
REMOTE=$(git remote -v | awk '/github\.com[:\/]RLinf\/RLinf(\.git)? \(fetch\)/ {print $1; exit}')
git fetch "$REMOTE" main "pull/$N/head:pr-$N"
BASE="$REMOTE/main"; PR_HEAD="pr-$N"
SKILLS="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.agents/skills"

gh pr view "$N" --repo RLinf/RLinf --json title,body,author,headRefOid,commits,files
gh pr checks "$N" --repo RLinf/RLinf
```
